lead.hed: U.S., Australian, Indian and Japanese navies open Malabar south of Honshu on Thursday
lead.insight: USNI News reports Malabar 2026 runs Nov. 5-12 in waters south of Japan's Kanto region, according to the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force. Last week, during the biennial U.S.-Japan exercise Keen Sword 27, USS Theodore Roosevelt exchanged sailors with an Australian frigate and passengers with a Canadian frigate.
lead.image_credit: MC2 Michael B. Jarmiolowski, U.S. Navy · DVIDS 7509212 · Public domain · USS Ronald Reagan steams with a Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force submarine during Exercise Malabar 2022, Philippine Sea, Nov. 11, 2022.

political.hed: Virginia votes Tuesday on three constitutional amendments, a U.S. Senate seat and 11 House seats
political.insight: The Department of Elections lists Sen. Mark Warner, a Democrat, against Republican Bert Mizusawa, and Rep. Rob Wittman, a Republican, against Democrat Shannon Taylor in the 1st District. Question 1 would protect decisions on abortion, birth control and fertility care while allowing third-trimester restrictions with exceptions. Question 2 would remove the state ban on same-sex marriage. Question 3 would automatically restore voting rights on release from incarceration. Polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m., and anyone in line at 7 may vote.

political.hed: Russia and North Korea both carried out ballistic missile launches last week
political.insight: USNI News reports Russia launched a submarine-launched ballistic missile from the Western Pacific to its Arctic region, citing a Russian Defense Ministry release, and that North Korea carried out a launch of its own. Russia has regularly carried out such launches from its Far East in October and November.

tech.hed: Australia reveals Ghost Shark payloads: sea mines, Altius-600 loitering munitions and supply caches
tech.insight: Officials showed the payloads Oct. 19 at Anduril Australia's Sydney factory, Defense News reports. A single extra-large undersea drone can lay a dozen mines. Canberra is spending A$1.7 billion (US$1.2 billion) on a fleet whose size it will not disclose, while it waits years for nuclear-powered submarines.

tech.hed: Google, OpenAI and Microsoft back one robots.txt rule to keep websites out of AI training
tech.insight: A shared policy token would let a site opt out across participating AI providers instead of writing separate rules for each crawler. The Internet Engineering Task Force draft comes from Kevin Kelley of Anthropic, who says the company has started work. Google aims to support it in 2027 and OpenAI in the coming months. Company-specific controls stay in place. Meta voiced support for a common signal without saying it would honor this one.
tech.source: Google Search Central / The Next Web

tech.hed: The Navy sent its first medium drone boat on an operational deployment with the Theodore Roosevelt strike group
tech.insight: Adm. James Kilby, the vice chief of naval operations, told the National Commission on the Future of the Navy on Oct. 8 that he wants drone-boat work written into ship certification exercises. He said he is not satisfied with the Navy's preparation for the medium unmanned vessels due to arrive, but believes the service has the structure it needs.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Madison's republic has room for both pluralism and virtue
culture.insight: Replying to Aaron Alexander Zubia's recent essay on James Madison, the writer argues that a diverse society and a virtuous one can stand together, and that Zubia's reading owes more to Richard Weaver than to Madison. The piece opens on Lincoln's Second Inaugural and closes on the American belief that people are capable of moral improvement.

culture.hed: Providence talks with Ken Adelman about the Reykjavik weekend that moved the Cold War
culture.insight: Editor-in-Chief Mark Tooley interviews Adelman about his new book, The Brink of War, on the October 1986 summit between Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev. Expected to be an empty grip-and-grin session, the weekend turned into a round of high-stakes negotiations.

watch.hed: The defense bill and full-year funding wait until after the midterms; the stopgap runs through Dec. 11
watch.note: Staff only. Military Times Oct. 22. Senate NDAA floor action put off until after the election; the stopgap also blocks new multiyear starts, including the F-35 framework that ran Oct. 22.
